dosing.evidence: saline or DOI (0.01, 0.03, 0.1, mg/kg, s.c.) was administered 15 minutes before the start of the self-administration session using a within-subjects, counterbalanced design. At least 72 hours occurred between DOI test days

group_housing.evidence: All rats were pair-housed with a same-sex cage mate in standard cages

day_night_flipped.evidence: The colony room was maintained on a 12-h light-dark cycle with lights on or off at 06:00 and 18:00, respectively. All procedures were conducted during the light cycle.

assays.assay_description: Operant self-administration of fentanyl in standard 2-lever Med-Associates chambers. FR1 acquisition (3-h daily sessions, 3.2 µg/kg/inf) followed by a low-price-twice within-session threshold procedure (2-h sessions, 11 doses descending by ¼ log every 10 min). DOI or saline administered 15 min pre-session in within-subjects design. Outcomes: active/inactive lever presses, infusions, consumption, latency, Q0 and α extracted from exponentiated demand function.

application_type.evidence: saline or DOI (0.01, 0.03, 0.1, mg/kg, s.c.) was administered 15 minutes before the start of the self-administration session

setup_habituation.evidence: Animals acquired fentanyl self-administration without prior food, magazine, or lever press training.

setup_restrain.evidence: A metal spring leash ... allowed unobstructed access to the entire operant chamber.

food_restriction.evidence: Standard chow food (LabDiet, Prolab RMH 3000) and water were available ad libitum, except during self-administration sessions.

water_restriction.evidence: Standard chow food ... and water were available ad libitum, except during self-administration sessions.

time_to_assay.evidence: DOI ... was administered 15 minutes before the start of the self-administration session

sample_size.evidence: n = 29; M = 16 received at least one dose, n = 13 for the 0.01 mg/kg, n = 15 for the 0.03 mg/kg, n = 16 for the 0.1 mg/kg; F = 13 received at least one dose, n = 13 for the 0.01 mg/kg, n = 12 for the 0.03 mg/kg, n = 13 for the 0.1 mg/kg

outcomes.summary: DOI dose- and sex-dependently altered fentanyl demand. In male rats, 0.01 mg/kg DOI increased demand intensity (Q0) and 0.1 mg/kg DOI increased demand elasticity (α). In female rats, 0.1 mg/kg DOI decreased Q0 but did not affect α. DOI did not alter inactive lever presses or latency to first active lever press.
outcomes.evidence: DOI dose-dependently altered fentanyl intake such that 5-HT2AR activation decreased Q0 in female rats but increased Q0 in male rats. For demand elasticity, DOI increased α in male rats but did not alter α in female rats.

B1_num_measures.evidence: active and inactive lever presses, total number of infusions, and consumption (µg) were all recorded ... demand elasticity (α) and demand intensity (Q0) ... latency to the first active lever press

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: infusions during each epoch were multiplied by the dose to yield µg consumed during that respective epoch ... consumption was plotted as a function of Price across 10-min epochs

B3_sequential_structure.evidence: no analysis of behavioural transitions or sequences reported

B4_ethological.evidence: behaviour measured was lever pressing, not natural ethological acts

B5_social.evidence: self-administration sessions were conducted in standard operant chambers with a single rat

B6_cognitive.evidence: operant self-administration on FR1 schedule requires instrumental learning

B7_automated_classification.evidence: Med-Associates lever-press hardware — beam-break/operant system, not a behavioural classifier

B8_multivariate.evidence: nonlinear mixed-effects modeling of demand parameters, not dimensionality reduction across behavioural features

E1_environment_type.evidence: standard operant chambers containing two retractable levers

E2_shelter.evidence: operant chamber provides no enclosed refuge

E3_bedding.evidence: standard operant chamber floor; no bedding described

E4_nesting.evidence: no nesting material in operant chamber

E5_enrichment.evidence: no enrichment objects in operant chamber

E6_spatial.evidence: single operant chamber compartment with two levers

E7_social_context.evidence: focal rat performed the task alone in the operant chamber

E8_food_water.evidence: food and water available ad libitum, except during self-administration sessions

D1_continuity.evidence: daily sessions across acquisition and within-session threshold testing; At least 72 hours occurred between DOI test days

D2_session_duration.evidence: daily three-hour sessions [acquisition] ... Eleven doses ... available across a two-hour session

D3_recording_days.evidence: daily three-hour sessions; 7 days per week during acquisition until stability, then within-session threshold procedure to stability, then 4 drug test days separated by ≥72 h

D4_baseline.evidence: There was no difference between Q0 or α across the saline treatment days and thus, those days were averaged.

D5_followup.evidence: DOI administered 15 min before each session; no ≥24 h post-acute behavioural recording reported

judge_notes: All three candidates agreed on a single operant self-administration assay; consolidated as one assay.
Schedule classified as 'repeated' rather than 'acute': within-subjects design with 4 DOI test days (vehicle + 3 doses) separated by ≥72 h.

D3_recording_days set to 15+ (score 3): acquisition required multiple days of daily 3-h FR1 sessions (stability across ≥3 consecutive days), threshold-procedure stability also required multiple days, plus 4 drug test days — clearly exceeds 14 recording days for this assay. Candidates underestimated this.
B1 set to 7+: paper reports active lever presses, inactive lever presses, total infusions, consumption (µg), Q0, α, and latency.
Sex top-level n_male/n_female reflect total subjects enrolled (18M/20F); assay sample_size reflects rats included in final analysis (16M/13F).
